sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling under identified treatment effects.
sampling_model.overlap: Known fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), imposed only on occupied cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The masses \(p_x\), propensities \(e_x\), and outcome regressions \(\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\) are all unknown; null cells, effect ties, and boundary outcome means are retained.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives the lower bound \(R^*(d,n)\gtrsim[d/(n\log n)]^2+1/n\) for a scalar regression mean when \(d\lesssim n\log n\).
Theorems 2.1--2.2 give matching sparse-regime \(W_1\) rates for a change law from independent parameter pairs observed through a common fixed number of binomial trials per arm.
Theorem 1 gives a near-sharp sorted \(\ell_1\) risk for an unlabeled discrete distribution using local moment matching and positive-measure reconstruction.
Corollary 2 bounds pointwise bias and variance for a smooth density-difference estimator with observed heterogeneous trial counts.

body.tldr: High-dimensional categorical adjustment makes every CATE location a difference of two armwise ratios, while the same unknown cell mass controls both sampling information and the atom's target weight.  On the unchanged observational model class, the paper proves the uniform logarithmic characterization \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d}\), the exact \(d/n\) dense frontier when \(n\ge d^3\), and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary, using the explicit total empirical probability-valued estimator for achievability.  The exact sparse-to-dense frontier remains open: grouped reconstruction is an explicit candidate blueprint, not a delivered estimator, until its split, tuning, factorial statistics, covariance control, finite program, fallback, and matching same-class converse are supplied.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal theory treats scalar averages, while population-of-parameters theory fixes entity weights or trial counts. Neither literature determines the squared \(W_1\) risk of the population-weighted categorical CATE law when masses, propensities, and both arm regressions are unknown.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied regime is a coupled multinomial-ratio inverse problem in which null cells and tied effects are legal and a valid output must be one coherent probability measure.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies observed-law identification, a mass-weighted Lipschitz extension, a computable total empirical probability-valued estimator, complementary same-class lower constructions, a uniform at-most-\(\log(ed)\) characterization with an explicit four-branch lower-benchmark phase diagram, the exact \(d/n\) dense frontier, and the bounded-category parametric-risk boundary.  It also states an explicit grouped moment-reconstruction blueprint for attacking the remaining gap, without presenting that blueprint as a constructed or rate-certified estimator.

body.related_work: Zeng et al. use the same observed categorical model class with unknown masses, propensities, and arm regressions, but their target is a scalar mean rather than the population CATE law.  Vinayak--Kong--Kakade study a different paired-binomial experiment with common fixed trials and equal entity weights; Han--Jiao--Weissman study a different one-population multinomial experiment and local sorted-distribution moments; and Lee--Bacak--Kennedy work in a different heterogeneous-trial regularity regime with observed trial counts and smooth mixing densities.  These papers motivate approximation, positive reconstruction, and sparse-to-dense comparisons, but none supplies the coupled unknown-mass observational frontier here.  Kennedy et al. concern smooth CATE-function loss, Chernozhukov et al. motivate effect-distribution reporting under regular sorting, and Mizuguchi--Sawamura provide the categorical-profile dexamethasone application; none changes the present target or closes its remaining logarithmic gap.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact frontier is not proved outside the dense branch: the current lower and upper bounds differ by at most \(\log(ed)\), and it is unknown which of the displayed \(n^{1/3}\), \(n^{1/3}\log(ed)\), and \(n\log(ed)\) elbows persist in the minimax rate.  The grouped reconstruction node is only a candidate blueprint.  It still requires an explicit split, shells, degree, grid, factorial statistic, exact covariance bound, feasibility tolerance, fallback, uniform Lipschitz-indexed risk proof, and matching same-class converse.  The early checks must retain unknown unequal weights, null cells, ties, and propensities at both overlap boundaries; a scalar-rate certificate contradicted by the separated-atom \(d/n\) floor must be rejected.
body.honest_scope: The target is the population law of conditional mean effects, not the law of individual potential-outcome differences, and Wasserstein recovery alone cannot certify an atom at zero.  What is proved is a same-class all-regime characterization within a factor of at most \(\log(ed)\), the exact \(d/n\) frontier for \(n\ge d^3\), the total empirical estimator's uniform risk bound, the stated one-sided consistency implications, and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary.  The exact sparse and transitional rate, the exact consistency region, the genuineness of the candidate phase elbows, and any rate guarantee for the grouped blueprint remain open.
